findings.summary: A normal worker calculation error was treated as a worker crash, rejecting all pending jobs and increasing the crash counter.
findings.root_cause: The worker onmessage ok:false branch called handleWorkerFailure(...), which terminates the worker and rejects every pending request. Calculation errors are per-request results and should not poison the worker bridge.
findings.fix: Changed the ok:false branch to settle only the matching pending request with an Error while keeping the live worker usable.
findings.regression: engine_validation_regression.py now scripts a worker that fails the first request and succeeds the second; the second request must resolve from the same live bridge path.

workflow_notes: Do not run sync_www-backed browser suites in parallel; they share the www staging directory and can create false missing-file failures.
The simplified V4 flow stayed focused: one real finding, one code fix, one targeted regression, then gates.
recommendations: Add a stable case ID for the new worker calculation-error bridge regression in a future registry cleanup pass.
Consider giving sync_www-backed browser tests isolated temp publish directories so they can safely run in parallel.
Keep export coverage tied to static/native/visual gates unless a concrete export bug appears; avoid adding broad slow browser traces without a behavioral reason.
